userStories.title: codex read-only mode; sandbox only where it is delivered
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give the `codex` registry entry read-only enforcement through its `read-only` mode and stop handing the embedder sandbox to agents that cannot receive it.

**Motivation** — `acpProfileFor` opens `read` or `review` for reviewers, re-reviewers and the advisor, but `unmetRequirement` refuses both on any agent without `readOnly` enforcement, so codex (which already has a `read-only` mode) can run implementer-shaped sessions only; and `routerFor` leaks the sandbox policy to codex, so `decidePermission` under `review` would approve a codex `execute` escalation as if it were sandboxed.

**Approach** —
Registry entry `codex` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/registry.ts`)
- Baseline (locates code only, never the interface): launch candidates and `authEnv: ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]`; `readOnly`, `defaultMode`, `preApproval` all undefined.
- Target: same launch, auth env, `defaultMode: undefined` and `preApproval: undefined`; `readOnly: { mode: { configId: "mode", value: "read-only" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {} }`. `entry()` takes the read-only enforcement without requiring a pre-approval channel. The `ReadOnlyEnforcement` doc comment drops "so only an agent with one may declare it" and says an agent may enforce read-only through its mode alone. Under `full` and `ask` codex keeps its launch mode (no `set_config_option` for `mode`).

`sandboxFor` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts`)
- Baseline: `sandboxFor(ctx: BackendOpenContext): SandboxPolicy | undefined` uses `ctx.sandbox` for profiles `review` and `full` and refuses the open when it is `unavailable`.
- Target: `sandboxFor(ctx: BackendOpenContext, entry: AgentRegistryEntry | undefined): SandboxPolicy | undefined`. Returns `undefined`, without refusing, when `entry?.preApproval` is undefined; otherwise behaves as the baseline. The caller in the open sequence passes `o.options.entry`.

`routerFor` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/backend.ts`)
- Baseline: `routerFor(ctx: BackendOpenContext, secrets: readonly string[]): InboundRouter` puts `sandbox: ctx.sandbox.policy` into the permission context whenever `ctx.sandbox.kind === "policy"`.
- Target: `routerFor(ctx: BackendOpenContext, secrets: readonly string[], entry: AgentRegistryEntry | undefined): InboundRouter`. Adds `sandbox` only when `entry?.preApproval` is defined and `ctx.sandbox.kind === "policy"`. Its caller in `connect()` passes `options.entry`. Elicitation answering shares the same base and reads no sandbox.

Symbols this story only reads (unchanged):
- `decidePermission(request, ctx)` in `permissions.ts`: under `review`, a non-`execute` request is rejected; an `execute` request is rejected with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON` when `ctx.sandbox` is undefined, otherwise allowed once with `REVIEW_EXECUTE_REASON`. Under `review` or `full` with `ctx.sandbox` defined, a network request is decided by `decideNetwork`. This feature changes what `ctx.sandbox` holds.
- `claudeSessionMeta(kind, toolNames, readOnly, extras)` in `pre-approval.ts` returns `undefined` unless `kind === "claudeCode.allowedTools"`.
- `modeFor(profile, entry)` in `capabilities.ts`: `none`/`read`/`review` -> `entry.readOnly.mode`, other profiles -> `entry.defaultMode`. `applyMode` in `open.ts` sets that mode through `session/set_config_option`, skips the call when the mode is undefined, and refuses with capability `profile` when the agent does not offer the value.

Failure handling:
- codex does not offer the mode value `read-only`: existing `applyMode` refusal, `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, capability `profile`, process killed.
- Profile `review` or `full` on codex with the embedder sandbox `unavailable`: the open proceeds; the unusable sandbox is not codex's to apply. (Claude still refuses as today.)
- codex asks to run a command outside its sandbox under `review`: rejected with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`.

Test support: add an exported `CODEX_CONFIG_OPTIONS` to `packages/nax-agent-acp/test/fixtures/fake-agent/script.ts` beside `CLAUDE_CONFIG_OPTIONS` (a `mode` select with category `mode` offering `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `agent`, `agent-full-access`, current value `agent`); no existing export changes. Put the integration tests in a new `packages/nax-agent-acp/test/unit/client/backend-codex.test.ts`, following the `inMemoryAgent` + `createAgentSession` pattern of `backend-permissions.test.ts`. Update the existing tests that assert the old codex shape (see expected test changes in the analysis).

**Scope** — In: codex registry entry, `entry()`, `ReadOnlyEnforcement` comment, `sandboxFor`/`routerFor` gating and their callers, fake-agent `CODEX_CONFIG_OPTIONS`, the new and adjusted tests in `packages/nax-agent-acp`. Out: embedder tools on codex (a session with tools is still refused with capability `tools`); applying nax's embedder sandbox to codex sessions or refusing codex escalations outside the workspace under `full`; anything in `packages/nax` (config schema, `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE`/`CODEX_HOME` env, `fullMode`, isolated home — all US-002); read-only enforcement for opencode, gemini and pi; Claude behaviour changes.

**Interface**
```typescript
// open.ts
function sandboxFor(ctx: BackendOpenContext, entry: AgentRegistryEntry | undefined): SandboxPolicy | undefined;
// backend.ts
function routerFor(ctx: BackendOpenContext, secrets: readonly string[], entry: AgentRegistryEntry | undefined): InboundRouter;
// registry.ts codex entry
readOnly: { mode: { configId: "mode", value: "read-only" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {} }
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `registryEntry("codex")?.readOnly` equals `{ mode: { configId: "mode", value: "read-only" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {} }`, and `registryEntry("codex")?.defaultMode` and `registryEntry("codex")?.preApproval` are both `undefined`.
[unit] Every registry entry whose `readOnly` is defined has a `readOnly.mode` with a non-empty `configId` and `value`.
[unit] `modeFor("read", registryEntry("codex"))`, `modeFor("none", registryEntry("codex"))` and `modeFor("review", registryEntry("codex"))` each equal `{ configId: "mode", value: "read-only" }`.
[unit] `modeFor("full", registryEntry("codex"))` and `modeFor("ask", registryEntry("codex"))` are both `undefined`.

[unit] `unmetRequirement(buildCapabilityRecord(init, registryEntry("codex")), { profile: "read", toolCount: 0, resume: false })` is `undefined`, where `init` is an `initialize` response with no MCP capabilities.
[unit] The same check with `profile: "review"` is `undefined`.

[integration] With a fake agent offering `CODEX_CONFIG_OPTIONS`, `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent: "codex", ... })` and profile `read` opens, and the fake records exactly one `session/set_config_option` call, with `configId` `"mode"` and `value` `"read-only"`.
[integration] The same codex open with profile `full` records no `session/set_config_option` call whose `configId` is `"mode"`.
[integration] A codex open with profile `read` sends `session/new` with `mcpServers: []` and no `_meta` field.
[integration] A codex open with profile `review` whose session carries a sandbox of kind `unavailable` opens without error.
[integration] A codex open with profile `full` whose session carries a sandbox of kind `unavailable` opens without error.

[integration] In a codex session opened with profile `review` and a sandbox of kind `policy`, a `session/request_permission` for an `execute` tool call is answered with the reject option, and the session records the decision `deny` with reason `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`.

[integration] In a Claude session opened with profile `review` and the same `policy` sandbox, the same `execute` permission request is answered with the `allow_once` option and recorded with reason `REVIEW_EXECUTE_REASON` (unchanged behaviour).
[integration] A Claude open with profile `review` and a sandbox of kind `unavailable` is still refused with `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, capability `profile`.

[integration] In a codex session opened with profile `read`, a `session/request_permission` for a file-edit tool call is answered with the reject option and recorded with reason `readOnlyReason("read")`.

[integration] A codex open with profile `read` whose fake agent offers a `mode` option without the value `read-only` is refused with `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, capability `profile`, and the agent process is killed once.
[integration] A codex open with profile `read` and one embedder tool is refused with `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, capability `tools` (unchanged).

[integration] In a codex session opened with profile `full` and a sandbox of kind `policy`, a `session/request_permission` for a file-edit tool call whose target lies outside the session's working directory is answered with the `allow_once` option and recorded with reason `FULL_REASON`.

routing.reasoning: Three source files in one package with a standard pattern, but the change decides which agents get sandbox-based permission approval (access control), so the security override requires strict test/implementation isolation.

suggestedCriteria: When a codex session opened with profile `review` and a sandbox of kind `policy` receives a `session/request_permission` for a file-edit tool call, the reject option is chosen.

modifiedFiles.reason: sets the codex entry's `readOnly`, lets `entry()` take read-only enforcement for an agent without pre-approval, and rewrites the `ReadOnlyEnforcement` comment that says only an agent with a pre-approval channel may declare it.
`sandboxFor` gains the `entry` parameter and returns `undefined` for an agent whose entry has no `preApproval`; its caller passes `o.options.entry`.
`routerFor` gains the `entry` parameter and omits `sandbox` from the permission context for an agent whose entry has no `preApproval`; its caller in `connect()` passes `options.entry`.

the table test "%s: launch candidates and auth env; no read-only enforcement, no pre-approval" asserts codex has `readOnly: undefined`, so codex moves out of that table into its own test asserting the new `readOnly` (gemini, opencode and pi stay in the table); and the test "only an agent with a pre-approval channel declares read-only enforcement" fails once codex declares `readOnly` without `preApproval`, so it is replaced by a test that every entry declaring `readOnly` sets a `readOnly.mode`, the invariant this feature relies on.

the test "modeFor and readOnlyFor: default mode for every Claude profile; nothing for agents without enforcement" asserts `readOnlyFor("none", registryEntry("codex"))` is undefined; that check switches to `registryEntry("gemini")`, keeping the invariant that an agent without enforcement yields undefined.

the test "%s on an agent without a read-only mode: refused after initialize" opens `agent: "codex"`; it switches to `agent: "gemini"`, keeping the invariant that `read`/`none` on an agent without read-only enforcement is refused after `initialize` with capability `profile`.

adds an exported `CODEX_CONFIG_OPTIONS` (a `mode` select with category `mode` offering `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `agent`, `agent-full-access`, current value `agent`) beside `CLAUDE_CONFIG_OPTIONS`; no existing export changes.

userStories.title: codex full mode and optional isolated home in nax
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Parsing a config with `agent.acp` unset yields `agent.acp.codex` equal to `{ isolateHome: false, fullMode: "workspace-write" }`.
[unit] Parsing a config with `agent.acp.codex.fullMode: "agent-full-access"` yields `"agent-full-access"`, and `agent.acp.codex.isolateHome` keeps its default `false`.
[unit] Parsing a config with `agent.acp.codex.fullMode: "danger"` fails validation with an issue whose path ends in `fullMode`.
[unit] Parsing a config with `agent.acp.codex.isolateHome: "yes"` fails validation with an issue whose path ends in `isolateHome`.

[unit] `codexAcpSettings(undefined)` returns `{ isolateHome: false, fullMode: "workspace-write" }`, and `codexAcpSettings({ agent: { acp: { codex: { isolateHome: true, fullMode: "agent-full-access" } } } })` returns `{ isolateHome: true, fullMode: "agent-full-access" }`.
[unit] `isolatedCodexHomeDir()` returns `join(globalConfigDir(), "acp", "codex-home")`.

[unit] With `_codexAcpEnvDeps` stubbed so `fileExists("/u/.codex/auth.json")` is true, `entryExists` is false for the isolated `auth.json`, `env("CODEX_HOME")` is undefined and `homedir()` is `"/u"`, `prepareIsolatedCodexHome()` calls `mkdir` with the isolated home, calls `symlink("/u/.codex/auth.json", <isolated>/auth.json)` once, and returns the isolated home.
[unit] With `env("CODEX_HOME")` returning `"/custom/codex"` and that `auth.json` present, the `symlink` target is `"/custom/codex/auth.json"`.
[unit] With `env("CODEX_HOME")` returning `""`, the source home is `<homedir()>/.codex`.
[unit] When `entryExists` is true for the isolated `auth.json` (including a dangling link), `prepareIsolatedCodexHome()` does not call `symlink` and returns the isolated home.
[unit] When `fileExists` is false for the source `auth.json`, `prepareIsolatedCodexHome()` calls `mkdir`, does not call `symlink`, and returns the isolated home.

[unit] `withCodexAcpEnv({ provider: "openai", model: "gpt", env: { A: "1" } }, "codex", { isolateHome: false, fullMode: "workspace-write" })` returns a new object whose `env` equals `{ A: "1", INITIAL_AGENT_MODE: "workspace-write" }`, the input's `env` still equals `{ A: "1" }`, and no `_codexAcpEnvDeps` filesystem function is called.
[unit] `withCodexAcpEnv(def, "codex", { isolateHome: false, fullMode: "agent-full-access" })` returns a def whose `env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` is `"agent-full-access"`.

[unit] `withCodexAcpEnv(def, "codex", { isolateHome: true, fullMode: "workspace-write" })` returns a def whose `env.CODEX_HOME` is the isolated home and whose `env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` is `"workspace-write"`.
[unit] `withCodexAcpEnv(def, "claude", { isolateHome: true, fullMode: "agent-full-access" })` returns `def` itself (same reference) and calls no `_codexAcpEnvDeps` function.

[unit] `withCodexAcpEnv({ provider: "openai", model: "gpt", env: { CODEX_HOME: "/mine", INITIAL_AGENT_MODE: "read-only" } }, "codex", { isolateHome: true, fullMode: "agent-full-access" })` returns a def whose `env` still has `CODEX_HOME` `"/mine"` and `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` `"read-only"`.

[unit] When `_codexAcpEnvDeps.mkdir` throws, `withCodexAcpEnv(def, "codex", { isolateHome: true, fullMode: "workspace-write" })` returns a def with no `CODEX_HOME`, with `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` `"workspace-write"`, and `_codexAcpEnvDeps.warn` is called exactly once.
[unit] `selectModel({ modelDef, agentName: "codex" })` (one argument) returns a `modelDef` whose env has neither `CODEX_HOME` nor `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE`.

[integration] `SessionManager.openSession` with `agentName: "codex"` and a config whose `agent.acp.codex` is `{ isolateHome: true, fullMode: "agent-full-access" }` calls the adapter's `openSession` with options whose `modelDef.env.CODEX_HOME` equals `isolatedCodexHomeDir()` and whose `modelDef.env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` is `"agent-full-access"`, with `_codexAcpEnvDeps` stubbed.

[integration] `SessionManager.openSession` with `agentName: "codex"` on a manager constructed with no config, and a request with no config, opens without throwing and passes `modelDef.env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` `"workspace-write"` and no `CODEX_HOME`.

[integration] `SessionManager.openSession` with `agentName: "claude"` and `isolateHome` `true` calls the adapter's `openSession` with a `modelDef` whose env has neither `CODEX_HOME` nor `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE`.

[integration] `completeAsWithFallback` with `agentName` `"codex"` and `input.config.agent.acp.codex` `{ isolateHome: true, fullMode: "workspace-write" }` calls `input.completeWithFallback` with options whose `modelDef.env.CODEX_HOME` equals `isolatedCodexHomeDir()` and `modelDef.env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` is `"workspace-write"`.

[integration] `completeAsWithFallback` with `agentName` `"codex"`, `input.config.agent.acp.codex.fullMode` `"workspace-write"` and `options.config.agent.acp.codex.fullMode` `"agent-full-access"` passes `modelDef.env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE` `"agent-full-access"` (the per-call config wins).

routing.reasoning: One new small module plus config and two one-line wiring edits following existing patterns (tracked-spawn-deadlines, selectModel); no security-sensitive decision logic, so a single TDD session suffices.

analysis:
Codex slice of nathapp-io/nax#2372. Two independent stories in two packages.

US-001 (packages/nax-agent-acp): codex-acp already offers a `mode` config option (read-only, workspace-write, agent, agent-full-access). Today the `codex` registry entry (src/client/registry.ts) has no `readOnly`, so `unmetRequirement` (src/client/capabilities.ts) refuses `read`/`review` with AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. Fix: give codex `readOnly: { mode: { configId: "mode", value: "read-only" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {} }`, leave `defaultMode` and `preApproval` undefined, and let `entry()` accept readOnly without a pre-approval channel (rewrite the ReadOnlyEnforcement doc comment). modeFor/applyMode are unchanged: none/read/review -> readOnly.mode; full/ask -> entry.defaultMode (undefined for codex, so no set_config_option for mode).
Sandbox leak: `sandboxFor` (src/client/open.ts) and `routerFor` (src/client/backend.ts) hand the embedder sandbox policy to `decidePermission` for every agent. codex never receives that policy (only Claude gets it via `_meta` / claudeSessionMeta), so under `review` an `execute` request would be allowed once as if sandboxed. Gate both on `entry?.preApproval`: sandboxFor(ctx, entry) returns undefined WITHOUT refusing when entry?.preApproval is undefined (so an `unavailable` sandbox no longer refuses codex review/full); routerFor(ctx, secrets, entry) adds `sandbox` to the permission context only when entry?.preApproval is defined and ctx.sandbox.kind === "policy". Callers pass `o.options.entry` (open sequence) and `options.entry` (connect()). decidePermission itself is unchanged: with ctx.sandbox undefined, a review `execute` is rejected with REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON; under full, file edits outside cwd are allowed with FULL_REASON (codex gets no stricter rule: the 'not too tight' ruling). Claude behaviour must not change (AC 13, 14).
Existing tests that break and must be updated (see Modifies): registry.test.ts (codex leaves the 'no read-only, no pre-approval' table; the 'only an agent with a pre-approval channel declares read-only' test is replaced by 'every readOnly entry has non-empty readOnly.mode'), capabilities.test.ts (readOnlyFor undefined check moves to gemini), backend-permissions.test.ts ('%s on an agent without a read-only mode: refused after initialize' switches agent codex -> gemini). Add exported CODEX_CONFIG_OPTIONS to test/fixtures/fake-agent/script.ts beside CLAUDE_CONFIG_OPTIONS (mode select, category `mode`, values read-only/workspace-write/agent/agent-full-access, current `agent`). New integration tests go in test/unit/client/backend-codex.test.ts, following the inMemoryAgent + createAgentSession pattern in backend-permissions.test.ts.

US-002 (packages/nax): add config `agent.acp.codex = { isolateHome: boolean=false, fullMode: "workspace-write"|"agent-full-access"="workspace-write" }` to AgentAcpConfigSchema (src/config/schemas-infra.ts, including its literal .default({...})), the literal acp default in src/config/schemas.ts, and the acp runtime type in src/config/runtime-types-agent.ts. New module src/agents/shared/codex-acp-env.ts (must live under src/agents/shared/, because src/agents/acp/ may not import config: check-adapter-no-config-import.sh) with CodexAcpSettings, codexAcpSettings (undefined-tolerant, precedent: src/config/tracked-spawn-deadlines.ts), isolatedCodexHomeDir (join(globalConfigDir(),"acp","codex-home")), prepareIsolatedCodexHome (mkdir recursive + symlink auth.json from $CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex, lstat semantics for the existing-entry check, fileExists via stat for source), withCodexAcpEnv (pure, returns a NEW def for agent "codex"; same reference for any other agent), and the _codexAcpEnvDeps test seam. INITIAL_AGENT_MODE=fullMode is set for every codex session; CODEX_HOME only when isolateHome; model-env values already present win; mkdir/symlink failure => one warn, no CODEX_HOME, still INITIAL_AGENT_MODE (fail open).
Wiring at the two places a model def enters an agent call: selectModel(opts, codex?) in src/session/model-selection.ts (ModelSelection gains optional agentName; one-arg call unchanged), called from SessionManager.openSession in src/session/manager.ts, where the single line `...selectModel(opts)` becomes `...selectModel(opts, codexAcpSettings(opts.config ?? this._config))` (manager.ts is at grandfathered size 650: replace one line, add none). completeAsWithFallback in src/agents/manager-complete-as.ts passes `{ ...options, modelDef: withCodexAcpEnv(options.modelDef, agentName, codexAcpSettings(options.config ?? input.config)) }` to buildCompleteCallPreamble (per-call config wins). manager-dispatch.ts (597/600 lines) must not be touched. Env flows through toSessionModel -> backendEnv(opts.modelDef.env) in src/agents/acp/open-context.ts -> buildAllowedEnv step 5 to the agent process, so no ACP-layer change is needed.
Also: update the profile-map.ts header comment (remove codex from the agents refused `read` until #2372; no code change), update agent-schema.test.ts 'agent.acp has no transport key after S4b-5' expected default to include the codex object, document both keys in docs/guides/configuration.md beside agent.acp.promptRetries (defaults, what fullMode chooses, isolateHome shares only auth.json).
Risks: file-size ratchets (manager.ts 650, manager-dispatch.ts 597/600) - do not grow; split tests across files if needed; existing tests that pin exact acp defaults; _deps restore idiom in tests (restore _codexAcpEnvDeps in afterEach); never bare `bun test`, run package test scripts. Packages are versioned in lockstep; no releases/version bumps in this feature.
The two stories are independent (no dependencies); US-001 touches only nax-agent-acp, US-002 only nax.
outOfScope: Read-only enforcement for opencode, gemini and pi (the rest of nathapp-io/nax#2372); this spec does not close that issue.

Applying nax's embedder sandbox to codex sessions, or refusing codex escalations outside the workspace under `full`: codex's own mode is its only boundary, every escalation it requests under `full` is approved with `FULL_REASON`, and nax's sandbox policy is never sent to it.
Profile `ask` on codex: it keeps codex's launch mode, which is now `agent.acp.codex.fullMode`; nax sets no mode for `ask`.
Embedder tools (the loopback MCP tool host) on codex: codex has no pre-approval channel, so a session with tools is still refused with capability `tools`.

Commands a codex reviewer runs that need temp-file writes or the network: they fail inside codex's read-only sandbox and the review reports them as it reports any failed command (accepted 2026-10-17).
Copying or translating any part of the user's codex config (hooks, MCP servers, plugins, skills, model providers) into the isolated home; only `auth.json` is linked.
Credentials kept in the OS keyring (`cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring"`): codex keys them by home path, so an isolated session does not find them.
A future codex release that saves `auth.json` by rename instead of in place would detach the link on the next token refresh; nax does not detect or repair that.
Turning `isolateHome` on or off moves where codex keeps its own session history, so a codex session started under the other setting cannot be resumed.
A `complete()` call that reaches codex only as a fallback agent: the fallback resolver supplies its own model def, so that call runs with codex's defaults (user home, mode `agent`).
Updating the package context file `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent-acp/context.md` to say codex is read-only capable: a manual step after merge, since `.nax/` is read-only to the run.
A billed live check against a real codex-acp process: a maintainer step after merge, modelled on phase C of `packages/nax-agent-acp/test/node/fixtures/live-claude-smoke.mjs`.
